review_notes: I read the whole file. I also checked the MulChar basics (`trivial` is `@[simps]`, `ringHomComp_one` is `@[simp]`, `ringHomComp_mul` and `ringHomComp_inv` are not) and the simp coverage in GaussSum.lean. The only simp lemma there is `gaussSum_one_one`. No `jacobiSum` lemma has any simp attribute, and `jacobiSum` is used only in this file. I found no competing rules, loops or wrongly oriented simp lemmas. The findings below are mild, since the file has no simp interface at all. I did not run Lean, so I cannot say whether the suggested attributes would cause problems with `simp`.

findings.excerpt: theorem jacobiSum_one_one : jacobiSum (1 : MulChar F R) 1 = Fintype.card F - 2 :=
findings.problem: The closed-form values of the Jacobi sum at the trivial character have no simp attribute, although the parallel Gauss-sum lemma `gaussSum_one_one` is `@[simp]`. Two versions are stated, `jacobiSum_trivial_trivial` (using `MulChar.trivial`) and `jacobiSum_one_one` (using `1`), and neither is simp. `1 : MulChar F R` is the `hasOne` instance and is not syntactically `MulChar.trivial F R`, so a simp call on `jacobiSum 1 1` cannot use the `trivial` version. In `exists_jacobiSum_eq_neg_one_add` the value is instead rewritten by hand, as in `rw [hχ₀, hψ₀, jacobiSum_one_one]`.
findings.proposed_change: Consider marking `jacobiSum_one_one` `@[simp]`, since it is the 1-based form that `simp` normal forms use. Keep `jacobiSum_trivial_trivial` as the non-simp underlying statement. The form `Fintype.card F - 2` is already in a simp-friendly shape. The `jacobiSum_one_nontrivial` lemma has a hypothesis `χ ≠ 1`, which `simp` can discharge from hypotheses. A simp attribute there is worth considering after checking the downstream uses.
findings.benefit: Goals that specialise to trivial characters, such as the `χ = 1`, `ψ = 1` case analysis in `exists_jacobiSum_eq_neg_one_add`, could be closed by `simp`. This matches the existing convention for `gaussSum_one_one`.

noncomputable instance hasOne : One (MulChar R R') :=
  ⟨trivial R R'⟩

findings.excerpt: jacobiSum (χ.ringHomComp f) (ψ.ringHomComp f) = f (jacobiSum χ ψ)
findings.problem: The only lemma relating `jacobiSum` to the other MulChar API has no simp attribute. Its LHS is a `jacobiSum` of two `ringHomComp`s, and its RHS is a ring homomorphism applied to a `jacobiSum` of the original characters. This is a natural normal-form direction: it moves `f` outside. Sibling lemmas such as `MulChar.ringHomComp_one` are simp. Yet `jacobiSum_mul_jacobiSum_inv` has to apply it manually with `rw [map_mul, ← jacobiSum_ringHomComp, ← jacobiSum_ringHomComp]`.
findings.proposed_change: Consider adding `@[simp]` to `jacobiSum_ringHomComp`. The LHS is a `jacobiSum` of two `ringHomComp`s, so it cannot loop. The change should be checked against the `ringHomComp_mul` and `ringHomComp_inv` rewrites at their call sites. The `←` rewrites in `jacobiSum_mul_jacobiSum_inv` would still be done by hand, since they go in the reverse direction.
findings.benefit: Statements that mix `jacobiSum` with `ringHomComp` would normalise to a single `f (jacobiSum χ ψ)` instead of requiring manual `rw`. This would also make the Jacobi-sum API consistent with `ringHomComp_one`.
